title: A bonus for {agent}?
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}, and the house made money.

choices.label: Pay {agent} a bonus of 30 dinars
choices.hint: It costs now. {agent} will remember it.

choices.label: Pay nothing more
choices.hint: The house keeps all of it.

note: Merchants paid an agent a wage or a share of the profit. An agent who did well was often sent out again.

sources.at: the Geniza letters, mostly 950 to 1250: merchants and their agents writing to each other

title: Out again, or rest?

choices.label: Send {agent} out again
choices.hint: The next sheet shows what sending {agent} costs.

choices.label: Let {agent} rest a season
choices.hint: A rested agent is glad of it.

note: Merchants paid an agent a wage or a share of the profit. An agent who did well was often sent out again.

sources.at: the Geniza letters, mostly 950 to 1250: merchants and their agents writing to each other

title: {agent} did not come back
body: {agent} was lost on the road to {to}.

choices.label: Help {agent}'s family
choices.hint: It costs now. The other agents hear of it.

choices.label: Do nothing more
choices.hint: The agents hear of that too.

note: Every trade road carried the risk of loss, so merchants split cargoes among ships and caravans and shared risk with partners.

sources.at: vol. 1, the economic foundations: how merchants spread risk

title: {agent} is safe
body: Part of the trip to {to} was lost, but {agent} is safe.

choices.label: Say it was no one's fault

note: Every trade road carried the risk of loss, so merchants split cargoes among ships and caravans and shared risk with partners.
